summary:
Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur's only documented item bearing on how a visibly non-conforming visitor may be policed in public space is a municipal swimwear order in Fréjus (Var). On 1 August 2023 the town's mayor, of the Rassemblement National, banned "covering and baggy clothing" while swimming from its sea beaches, in force until 17 September 2023, with a €135 fine.

The administrative court of Toulon suspended the order's execution on 5 August 2023 and ordered the commune to pay €3,000. In freedom-of-relief order n° 2302537, brought by the Ligue des droits de l'homme, the court held the arrêté to be a grave and manifestly unlawful attack on fundamental freedoms: the manifestation of religious conviction, freedom of movement, and freedom of dress in public space.

The mayor's communiqué justified the ban by laïcité while public statements cited safety, and observers read the measure as aimed at religiously marked swimwear. The suspension is interim relief; it prevents enforcement of the order.

No other region-specific measure, enforcement practice or incident affecting transgender visitors appears in the inventory, and the national assessment applies to the region.
tangentialFactors:
The Toulon court followed the Conseil d'État's ruling of 17 July 2023 on an identical arrêté at Mandelieu-la-Napoule (Alpes-Maritimes), also in this region. The Ligue des droits de l'homme contested that measure as well.

Municipal dress codes of this kind are not trans-specific instruments. Their bearing on a trans visitor is that they place enforcement discretion over public dress and appearance in the hands of municipal police on beaches, and that the courts have treated freedom of dress in public space as a fundamental freedom that such orders cannot override.
localsOnly:
Residents of Fréjus and Mandelieu-la-Napoule have lived under municipal swimwear bans adopted in 2023. Both were challenged by the Ligue des droits de l'homme, and the Fréjus commune was ordered to pay the organisation €3,000.

The Conseil d'État's 17 July 2023 ruling on the Mandelieu-la-Napoule arrêté gives residents a basis for contesting comparable municipal orders in this region.
outOfScopeNotes:
The inventory does not record whether the commune of Fréjus appealed the suspension or whether the case on the merits concluded, so the order's final status is unresolved.

No region-specific data on trans-specific enforcement, incidents, facilities, screening or care access in Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur appears in the inventory.

The swimwear orders are not trans-specific measures. The inventory records no instance of a transgender person stopped or fined under them, so their bearing on transgender visitors is indirect and rests on the discretion they confer rather than on documented enforcement against trans people.
